title: Capacity Commitment Bands + Burst Credits: experiment & SQ onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Proposal and experimental plan for a multi-tier dedicated GPU offering that combines: (1) capacity commitment bands (monthly reserved GPU units), (2) a burst-credit pool for short-term scaling, and (3) autoscale policies with fallback to preemptible devices and fallthrough SLAs. The goal is to surface a simple product matrix that sales can pitch to enterprise customers with predictable unit economics, clear overage behavior, and a documented security/questionnaire path for Private deployments. This ticket owns: pricing experiments, contract language templates for entitlements and overage, SQ answers for dedicated/private deployment, and validation with a small set of pilot customers.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: Aligned on scope with Eng (Marco), Legal (J. Rivera), Sales (Priya), Solutions (Diego). Agreed success metrics: (A) <5% revenue churn vs expected after 90 days from pilot, (B) p99 token latency within committed SLA for 95% of traffic during normal load, (C) burst usage remains >80% self-contained within credit pool for pilot customers.

2026-02-18 - Early modeling: Finance ran unit economics for 3 band sizes (Small/Med/Large). Example: Small band = 4 reserved T4-like GPUs -> effective per-hour cost discounted 35% vs on-demand; burst credits enabled 2x short-term capacity for up to 12 hours per week. Trade-off: smaller bands have worse tail cost; we propose a flat surcharge for overage rather than per-GPU minute billing to simplify sales conversations.

2026-02-24 - Eng feedback (ENG-41200): Autoscaler prototype supports aggressive scale-up with warm KV cache reuse for compatible models but requires a short warm-up delta at first scale event (~2–4s p95 additional latency). Decided to include a documented pre-warm window in SLA language for initial burst events.

2026-03-02 - Legal review: Draft contract language prepared. Key changes requested: define 'burst credit consumption' and 'grace throttling', clarify data residency obligations for Private deployments. Legal asked for a Security Questionnaire (SQ) stub to be completed before any on-prem demo. Assigned to Security to own SQ answers but product must produce the orchestration flow diagram.

2026-03-06 - Solutions engineering ran two pilot configurations against customer sample workload (ecommerce chat + embedding store). Results: burst pool consumed 72% in week 1, tuned autoscale to prioritize KV-cache friendly replicas to avoid cold starts. Issue logged ENG-41876 to add cache-transfer optimization in scale path.

2026-03-10 - Sales pilot acceptance: Customer A (mid-market) approved pilot contract with Small band + 1-month trial. Sales requested a one-page 'what to expect' for support ops during pilot. Draft created at https://drive.redwood.ai/pilot-one-pager/PM-880432.

2026-03-12 - Stakeholder sync: Agreed to run 3 pilots (mid-market, fintech, health-care partner). Added a monitoring dashboard with burst credit burn rate and autoscale events: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/credits/pm-880432. Next milestone: deliver SQ answers and update SLA text to include pre-warm allowance and credit exhaustion policy.

2026-03-12 - Risk: If cache-transfer optimization (ENG-41876) slips >2 sprints, initial pilot may see p99 spikes that could invalidate SLA promises. Mitigation: conservative default SLA for pilot customers + feature flag to disable aggressive autoscale for those without cache-transfer support.
decision_history: 2026-02-11 - Decided to run tiered bands instead of fully metered GPU minutes to reduce negotiation complexity with enterprise procurement.
2026-02-24 - Chose flat overage surcharge model for initial pilots to produce predictable invoice items (legal/sales aligned).
2026-03-02 - Included a documented 60s 'pre-warm' allowance in SLA for the first scale event; not counted as SLA breach if observability shows KV cache misses during window.
2026-03-06 - Agreed to include an 'autoscale opt-out' flag for customers that require deterministic latency and are willing to pay a premium.
2026-03-12 - Pilot cohort defined: 3 customers across industries; only pilot customers will get a 30-day forgiveness window on burst overage while we tune policy.
acceptance_criteria: Billing prototype emits band + credit usage lines to billing export

Monitoring dashboard shows credit-burn, scale-events, and cache-warm metrics for pilot customers

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected high burst consumption leading to customer surprise invoices - Mitigation: implement soft alerts and 30-day forgiveness for pilots
Risk: Autoscale cold-starts create p99 spikes - Mitigation: pre-warm SLA allowance and conservative autoscale thresholds until ENG-41876 deployed
Risk: SQ gaps delay on-prem demos - Mitigation: prioritize SQ stub answers and host architecture diagram to Security for immediate review
